results.evidence: `resolve_untagged_followup_mode` now returns `UntaggedFollowupMode(stored) if stored else UntaggedFollowupMode.ASK` for a missing row or empty column. The activity then falls through to `_post_untagged_followup_prompt` when mode is ASK. The webhook gate isn't shown, but it reads the same resolver.
Stored auto, ask and never values are still returned as-is by the resolver. The activity still returns False for AUTO and True with no prompt for NEVER. Nothing in the patch changes those branches.

The prompt keeps `UNTAGGED_FOLLOWUP_ACTION_RUN` and `UNTAGGED_FOLLOWUP_ACTION_DISMISS`. With `offer_default` it adds "Always pick up my replies" and "Never pick up my replies" buttons. These call `_save_untagged_followup_default` with AUTO or NEVER, stored under the replier's own row.

`_untagged_followups_section_blocks(mode)` renders an initial option from whatever mode it is given, and the patch changes only its docstring. The caller that decides whether to include the section isn't shown, so I can't tell whether it is omitted for users with no row.

`_stored_untagged_followup_mode` returns `stored if stored in UntaggedFollowupMode.values else None`. The resolver then maps None to `UntaggedFollowupMode.ASK`. An unrecognised stored value therefore now resolves to ASK and starts prompting, where before it resolved to NEVER. The docstring even says "a value we no longer recognise all resolve to `ASK`".

The prompt's context text is a plain string: "You can change it any time from the PostHog app's Home tab." It has no link, and it doesn't use `app_home_url` (which is imported in api.py) or any fallback logic.
The patch has no quota-related changes. Nothing suppresses the quota-denial message for unconfirmed untagged replies.

result:
A Slack user with no saved thread follow-up setting is now asked whether their untagged reply should go to the agent. I haven't run the tests or the linter, as you asked, so none of this is checked.

- **Default:** an unset setting used to resolve to "never", which is why the reply was dropped without a prompt. It now resolves to "ask" (`services/slack_settings.py`).
  - Unset includes a missing row, an empty value and a retired value.
  - If the creator can't be identified, it still resolves to "never".
  - Users who already picked auto, ask or never behave as before.
  - The existing flow does the rest: the webhook lets the reply through, the classifier judges it, and the workflow posts the private "Want me to pick up your message?" prompt.
- **Save a default from the prompt:** when the person replying has no saved setting, the prompt also shows "Always pick up my replies" and "Never pick up my replies".
  - "Always" saves auto and runs this reply.
  - "Never" saves never and drops it.
  - The plain Yes and No buttons still save nothing.
  - The changes are in `api.py` and `activities/messaging.py`, plus a new `has_untagged_followup_preference` helper.
- **Home tab:** the Thread follow-ups picker already existed, so I didn't change its behavior. An unset user now sees "Ask them first" there instead of "Leave them alone", which matches the new default. I updated the docstrings and comments in `models.py` and `slack_app_home.py` to match.

I flipped the expectations for the unset case in `test_slack_settings.py` and `test_thread_message_routing.py`. I also added two cases to `test_request_untagged_followup_confirmation_activity.py`, one for offering the save buttons when nothing is saved and one for not offering them otherwise. The new button handlers have no tests.

The setting still governs threads the person started, and the saved default is stored under whoever clicks the button. If someone replies in a thread another person started, "Always" or "Never" changes the replier's own setting, not the thread creator's. Say if you'd rather it did something different there.
